brief.ask: Art-direct "Frankincense & Gold Dust" — #10 of the 72 Ambo church visualizers (Calm Contemporary Worship lyric visualizer, Collection I of 72; subgenre Contemplative Light). Premise: Swinging brass thurible censer, aromatic smoke plumes, and diagonal altar beam. An ornate brass thurible censer swings gently in the upper sanctuary while silky curls of liturgical incense rise through a diagonal shaft of warm amber altar light. Lighting today: Key: Single diagonal 3400K altar spot cutting through dark nave. Service use: Prayer, intercession, Sanctus, contemplative worship. Audio mapping today: Swell → Widens the ascending incense smoke curl & altar beam; Vocal → Brightens the swinging brass thurible censer & smoke scattering; Shimmer → Drifts fine suspended gold dust motes. Palette: #09080C #241B18 #D49448 #FFF2DC. Keep the id, name, premise and palette; rebuild the direction: the geometry and depth planes, typography for the worship lyric band (one line at a time, four to five seconds a line, word-by-word progression), image logic (how the procedural scene (no concept plate: the plate is generative, in code) and the procedural scene meet), texture, motion, and which audio channel drives what. Decide it — the lead's lens will drive the kit's material weave and optical pass for this one.
brief.audience: Congregations watching a projector or LED wall from the pews, five to forty metres away, eyes on the words; and the worship leader or volunteer running Ambo live from a laptop.
brief.feeling: Stillness and reverence — a sanctuary that breathes with the singer's voice; gorgeous, slow, never a screensaver.
constraints: Build method (fixed): a real-time Canvas 2D audio-reactive renderer in Plajah's worship visualizer kit — sanctuary background, multi-plane depth (god rays, motes, bokeh), the kit's Council optical pass (35mm light leaks, anamorphic flare, film grain, colour punch, and a tactile material weave keyed to the LEAD director's lens) and the kit's lyric / scripture typography engine. No video playback, no WebGL, no assets beyond the one concept plate.

Audio drives amplitude, colour, light, growth and glow only — never the position of the words. Envelopes are smoothed; nothing strobes or flashes (photosensitive-safe); uptempo pulses are spring-damped.

The reading band is sacred: lyrics or scripture must stay legible at 1920×1080 and 4K from the back pew, over the busiest moment of the scene. A text-safe dimming band is part of the kit; direct how the scene yields to it.

Typefaces are fixed to the kit's open-licensed set: Noto Serif (text serif), Outfit / Inter (sans), Cinzel (display), JetBrains Mono. Direct scale, case, tracking, measure and hierarchy, not new families.

Sacred imagery is used correctly and respectfully: biblical places and objects are specific and attributable, never costume; nothing denominational or branded; nothing that reads as a music video or a screensaver.
Runs at 60 fps on an integrated-GPU laptop driving a projector: favour layered gradients, cached textures and a few large shapes over particle storms.
Keep this visualizer's id, name, premise and four-colour palette. The council owns the direction, not the catalogue entry.
references: No concept plate: the scene is built entirely in code from the premise.
Sample lyric lines on the band: "Be still my soul the Lord is on thy side" / "Bear patiently the cross of grief or pain".

proposals.title: Cantus Firmus in Amber
proposals.idea: The thurible's pendulum arc is the governing measure — every depth plane, smoke curl, and lyric interval is derived from a single φ-proportioned swing period, so the scene breathes in one structural voice.
proposals.geometry: The canvas is divided by a φ-spine (x = 0.618W) and a luma-grid of 24×14 nodes inherited from the procedural background — these two authorities, and no others, place every element. The diagonal altar beam runs from upper-left at 23° (a Pythagorean 5:12 slope, not an arbitrary rake), crossing the φ-spine at the vertical golden point (y = 0.382H); this intersection is the compositional fulcrum from which the thurible hangs. Three depth planes are declared before any content: Plane 1 (rearmost) — the dark nave gradient, nearly black at #09080C bleeding to #241B18, occupies the full field and is the cantus firmus of the luma-grid; Plane 2 — the altar beam and smoke column, constrained to the corridor between x = 0.45W and x = 0.72W; Plane 3 (foremost) — the thurible body, held within a bounding ellipse whose semi-major axis is exactly one-third of canvas height, centered on the φ-spine at y
proposals.typography: Cinzel Regular, sentence case, set at a type scale derived from the same φ-ratio governing the geometry: display size = 0.048H (≈ 52px at 1080p), tracked at +0.12em, measure capped at 0.72W centred on the φ-spine. One lyric line at a time. Word-by-word progression: each word fades in over 18 frames (300 ms at 60 fps) on a cubic ease-in-out — not a pop, a breath; preceding words hold at full opacity; the completed line holds for the remainder of its 4–5 s window then dissolves in 24 frames. No bold weight — Cinzel's incised Roman capitals carry authority through proportion, not mass. Baseline sits at y = 0.84H (centred in the text-safe band). A text-safe dimming band renders as a radial luma mask: luminance of all scene layers is clamped to ≤ 0.12 within 40px of the baseline, widening to the full band width; the mask is soft-edged with a 60px feather so the scene does not visibly cut. proposals.texture: The optical pass runs as a Canvas 2D composite layer drawn last, at globalCompositeOperation 'screen' or 'overlay' depending on zone. Film grain: a 256×256 tileable noise texture (pre-generated at build time, owned asset) scrolls at 1px/frame on both axes — amplitude 0.04 over the full field, rising to 0.07 in the smoke column to simulate the granular scatter of real incense particle light. The material weave keyed to the Classical lens is linen-register: a horizontal hatching pattern at 1px stroke, 8px pitch, 3% opacity — visible only in the mid-tone nave zone (#241B18 region), not in the beam or text band, so it reads as substrate without competing with legibility. The anamorphic streak is a single 1px-high horizontal line at the thurible's specular peak, spanning x = 0.30W to x = 0.80W, colour #FFF2DC at 0.55 opacity, masked to zero within the text-safe band; it does not drift or puls
proposals.motion: The thurible pendulum is the governing clock. Swing period T = 3.6 s (a pendulum of plausible sanctuary length, computed from L ≈ 3.2 m: T = 2π√(L/g)), implemented as a damped cosine: θ(t) = θ₀ · e^(−0.04t) · cos(2πt/T), where θ₀ = 14°. The thurible body rotates with θ; the chain segments (6 links, cached) follow with a 40 ms lag per link — this is not spring physics, it is a fixed-offset echo, predictable and re-readable. All other motion is derived from T or its φ-subdivision (T/φ ≈ 2.22 s): smoke ribbons shift their Bézier control points on a 2.22 s cycle; the altar beam's opacity breathes on a 3.6 s cycle in phase with the swing. Audio mapping — Swell channel (low-frequency amplitude envelope, smoothed over 180 ms): widens the altar beam polygon by up to +0.08W and raises smoke ribbon opacity by +0.06 — the sanctuary inhales with the congregation's sustained notes. proposals.productionMethod: Real-time Canvas 2D renderer in Plajah's worship visualizer kit. Build sequence: (1) Declare cantus firmus constants in an exported JS module — φ, T, luma-grid dimensions, palette hex values, text-safe band coordinates, beam angle — before any draw call; these are immutable at runtime. (2) On init, pre-render three OffscreenCanvas caches: thurible path (512×512), grain tile (256×256), linen-hatch tile (128×128). (3) Each frame at 60 fps: clear → draw Plane 1 nave gradient → draw altar beam polygon → draw 14 smoke ribbons (Bézier, updated from Perlin field + audio Swell) → draw 48 motes (audio Shimmer scales radius/opacity only) → draw thurible from cache with rotation transform → composite optical pass (grain scroll, linen-hatch, anamorphic streak, light-leak vignette) → apply text-safe luma mask → draw lyric band (Cinzel, word-by-word, clock-driven). Audio analysis: Web Audio API Analys
proposals.humanTrace: The governing measure — the 3.6 s swing period — is physically derived from a plausible sanctuary pendulum length, not chosen for aesthetic feel; the damping coefficient is tuned so the thurible loses arc over four minutes of continuous motion, as a real thurible would if not re-swung. The smoke ribbon Perlin field is seeded with a value hand-selected by the art director after observing which seed produces a curl that reads as liturgical incense rather than steam or fog — that editorial choice is the human mark. The linen-hatch opacity is set by eye at 3%, confirmed against a projected test frame at 8 metres, to be perceptible as substrate without competing with the text — that calibration is craft, not algorithm.
proposals.risk: The φ-governed geometry and pendulum-derived timing produce a scene of exceptional structural coherence — but if the worship leader's song tempo happens to phase-lock with the 3.6 s swing (a 4/4 hymn at ≈ 67 BPM), the visualizer may read as mechanically choreographed rather than spiritually breathed. The risk is worth carrying because the alternative — arbitrary timing — produces a scene that cannot be read twice the same way and therefore cannot hold a congregation in stillness; a structure that occasionally rhymes with the music is not a failure of proportion but a confirmation of it.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the smoke to surge on the Swell peak and the thurible to flare its specular highlight at the Vocal climax — a reveal that announces itself. I am directing against that: the smoke widens by 0.08W, not billows; the highlight rises from 0.55 to 0.85, not to a white flash. The scene must not perform its emotion. proposals.title: Ink Lifted Into Light
proposals.idea: The thurible's arc is a registration mark — every smoke curl, every mote, every lyric baseline answers to that one prior physical decision, so the scene carries the evidence of a single swinging weight rather than a mood it borrowed.
proposals.geometry: One declared polar anchor: thurible pivot at 38% from top, 50% horizontal. From that anchor, a single swing arc (±22° from vertical, period ~4.2 s, eased sinusoidal, never fully stopping) governs everything — the diagonal altar beam is locked to 34° off vertical, originating from upper-left at 15% / 8%, striking the nave floor at 82% / 94%; the smoke column rises from the censer's bowl position (recomputed each frame from swing state) along a vector that is always 12° counter to the beam, so beam and smoke are permanently in productive argument; bokeh motes are seeded only inside the beam trapezoid, their y-positions drawn from a 24×14 luminance grid sampled from the rendered beam gradient, authorised above luma 0.32; the lyric band occupies a fixed horizontal strip, 72%–88% of frame height, full width, so the text baseline is always below the swing arc and never competes with the censer
proposals.typography: Cinzel for the lyric line — uppercase, tracked at +0.12 em, set at fluid clamp between 3.2 vw and 52 px minimum; one line visible at a time, centred, optical margin alignment on; word-by-word reveal: each word fades in over 18 frames (0.3 s at 60 fps), the previous word dims to 55% opacity but stays on screen so the phrase accumulates, then the whole line dissolves over 24 frames before the next line seeds; the text-safe dimming band is a full-width radial-gradient panel, #09080C at 72% opacity, spanning the lyric strip plus 4% above and below — it is always present, intensity never dropping below 65% opacity regardless of audio state; scripture / secondary label in Noto Serif Italic, 1.4 vw, #FFF2DC at 60% opacity, sitting 1.8 line-heights below the lyric baseline; no mixed-case, no sentence-case — Cinzel earns its register or it doesn't run.
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate, no imported asset. The scene is constructed entirely in Canvas 2D from declared constants: (1) the beam is a Path2D trapezoid filled with a three-stop linear gradient (#FFF2DC at 18% opacity at origin, #D49448 at 9% at midpoint, transparent at terminus), redrawn each frame with the censer's current swing angle baked in; (2) the thurible censer is a procedural silhouette — stacked ellipses and a spline chain for the chain links, stroke in #D49448, line width 1.5 px, with a candle-flicker Perlin luminance oscillating 0.3–1.8 Hz applied to its fill opacity; (3) smoke is a stack of eight Bezier curves emitted from the bowl's computed position, each curve's control points drifting on low-frequency Perlin noise (octave 2, persistence 0.45), drawn with a radial gradient stroke from #FFF2DC at 6% to transparent, new curve added every 90 frames and oldest dropped; (4) motes are
proposals.texture: Film grain is a full-frame Canvas noise pass: 120×68 px offscreen canvas of random greyscale pixels, scaled up 16× with imageSmoothingEnabled false, composited at 'overlay' blending mode, 8% opacity — this is the paper tooth, present always, never keyed to audio, never decorative, it is the material witness that the scene was rendered not painted-over; a second pass adds anamorphic lens streak: two horizontal linear-gradient lines at 0.5 px height, positioned at the beam's entry point, #FFF2DC at 22% opacity at centre fading to transparent over 18% of frame width, their x-position jittered ±1 px per frame from Perlin noise to read as physical rather than computed; foil shimmer on the thurible silhouette is a highlight arc redrawn each frame with highlight vector locked to 35° (matching beam angle declared in geometry), luminance oscillating with the candle-flicker shader — the shimmer is

proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer, 60 fps, single render loop. Offscreen canvas for nave gradient (cached). Offscreen canvas for film grain tile (refreshed every 3 frames to cut cost). Procedural censer silhouette drawn with Path2D, cached and translated/rotated from pivot each frame — no redraw of the path itself unless swing angle changes more than 0.05 rad. Smoke Bezier stack: eight curves in a ring buffer, control points stored as typed Float32Arrays, updated with a single Perlin octave per frame. Motes: 72 objects in a pre-allocated array, positions updated in a tight loop with no garbage. Lyric engine: word tokens pre-split at load, rendered to an offscreen canvas per line-change, composited with globalAlpha — no per-frame text layout. All Perlin calls use a 256-entry permutation table seeded once at load. Total draw calls per frame: nave composite (1), beam path (1), smoke curves (8 strokes), mo
proposals.humanTrace: The swing arc period (4.2 s) and amplitude (±22°) were declared before any other constant — they are the first human decision, equivalent to setting registration on a press before the plate goes down. Every downstream position — smoke origin, beam angle, mote seed grid — is computable only after that declaration. The grain tile is refreshed every 3 frames at 120×68 px and scaled up rough: the pixel boundary is visible at projection scale and that roughness is kept, not smoothed, because it is the evidence that something was rendered not illustrated. The candle-flicker Perlin seed is fixed at load from a declared integer (seed 1847) — the same flicker pattern plays every service, which means a worship leader running this twice in a week will notice the censer breathes the same way, like a physical object in a room they know.
proposals.risk: Cinzel uppercase at this scale in a dark sanctuary reads as proclamation, not whisper — if the worship context is genuinely contemplative the type may feel too authoritative for the moment. That risk is worth carrying because the alternative is a face that disappears into the scene, and from forty metres the lyric must win or the whole kit fails its primary job. The grain tile at 8% overlay on a dark palette may read as compression artifact on a consumer projector with low contrast ratio — the counter is that it is the only texture that proves the scene was made rather than generated, and losing it would be the more serious failure.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the smoke to billow wider, the beam to pulse harder on vocal peaks, the censer to glow with more saturation — drama earned through excess. I say the restraint in the lerp coefficients and the opacity floors is not timidity, it is the difference between a sanctuary that breathes and a light show that performs breathing. proposals.title: Luminance Field With Liturgical State
proposals.idea: The scene is a single generative light-transport equation — thurible angle, smoke density, beam width, and mote drift are all continuous outputs of one shared amplitude state vector, so the sanctuary does not react to the music so much as it IS the music, re-solved every frame.
proposals.geometry: Three depth planes, each a discrete z-layer with no overlap blending except at governed composite boundaries. Plane 0 (background): a 1920×1080 radial gradient from #09080C at corners to #241B18 at a displaced center — center position is a slow Lissajous drift (period ~40s) that the audio state cannot interrupt, only modulate ±4 px amplitude. Plane 1 (god-ray / beam): a single diagonal shaft, entry at upper-left 28% of frame width, exit at lower-right 72%, painted as a sequence of 7 overlapping additive-blend Gaussian strips at 3400K (#D49448 at core, #FFF2DC at specular ridge) — each strip has an independent width parameter w_i driven by Swell amplitude envelope; at silence w_i = base constant, at full swell w_i expands to 1.6× via a spring with k=0.18, damping=0.72. Plane 2 (foreground motes): a 160-point particle field, each mote a pre-cached 32×32 radial gradient sprite; mote positio
proposals.typography: Lyric band uses Cinzel for the active line — uppercase, tracking 0.18em, size 52px at 1080p (scales to 104px at 4K via viewport ratio), centered, max-width 72% of frame to prevent line breaks on short liturgical phrases. Word-by-word progression: each incoming word fades in over 180ms (opacity 0→1, no translate), sits at full weight, then the previous word drops to 40% opacity but does not leave — the full line accumulates word by word as a dimming trail until line change, at which point the whole line cross-fades out over 320ms and the next line initialises. This is not a slide; it is a continuous luminance accumulation that mirrors the incense build. Line duration 4–5 seconds, word timing computed from line duration ÷ word count with a minimum 600ms per word. Scripture reference (if shown) uses Noto Serif Italic, 24px at 1080p, tracking 0.06em, positioned at 84% vertical, 20% opacity —
proposals.imageLogic: There is no concept plate. The scene is a closed generative system: all visual elements are computed geometry, gradient fields, and pre-cached sprite textures generated at renderer init from parametric descriptions. The 'photograph' this system is citing is the physics of a 3400K tungsten spotlight passing through a smoke-filled nave — that is the simulation target, not a mood reference. The light-transport model is explicit: beam luminance falls off as 1/r² from the shaft axis (approximated with a Gaussian whose σ is a function of Swell amplitude); mote scatter is approximated by additive compositing of the mote sprites at opacity proportional to their distance from the beam axis inverted — motes inside the beam are brighter, motes outside are nearly invisible. This is not a photograph of light; it is a rule about what light does, running in real time.
proposals.texture: The Council optical pass for this card is driven by The Futurist lens: film grain is a generated 512×512 tileable luminance-noise texture, baked at init from a seeded PRNG, scrolled at 0.5 px/frame diagonally — it does not animate frame-by-frame (no per-frame noise regeneration, GPU budget preserved). Grain intensity is fixed at 6% opacity additive over the composite — it does not pulse with audio. Anamorphic flare: a single horizontal streak across the beam's specular ridge, 3px tall, 40% of frame width, rendered as a linear gradient from transparent to #FFF2DC 18% opacity and back — it is a static overlay keyed to beam geometry, not a separate animation. Colour punch: a multiply-blend vignette using #09080C at 35% opacity, elliptical, 1.15× frame width — this is what makes the field feel like a lens, not a canvas. No light-leak animation. No lens-blur bokeh on motes — motes are small e
proposals.motion: Initialisation (0–800ms): background gradient resolves from black; beam strips fade in sequentially from upper-left to lower-right at 80ms intervals — this is the only staged reveal; everything after is steady-state. Steady state is the primary specification. Thurible: continuous damped cosine swing, period ~6.4s, amplitude ±9° at rest; Vocal envelope adds up to ±4° via spring (k=0.22, d=0.65) — the censer is always moving, audio modulates the amplitude of an already-living system, it does not start or stop it. Smoke splines: recomputed each frame, control points drift upward at base rate 0.04 px/frame; Swell amplitude fans the lateral spread of upper control points; the visual result is a slow widening and narrowing of the plume that breathes with the harmonic swell — no new paths spawn, the three paths are always present. proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer, 60fps target. Init phase: generate grain texture (512×512, seeded noise, once); rasterise thurible silhouette to offscreen canvas (once); rasterise 160 mote sprites to offscreen canvas strip (once, 32×32 each, radial gradient #D49448 to transparent). Frame loop: clear with background gradient (radial, 2 stops); composite beam strips (7 drawImage or fillRect with globalAlpha, additive); composite smoke splines (3 strokePath calls, feathered, additive); composite thurible offscreen canvas at computed transform (translate + rotate); composite mote sprites (160 drawImage calls, pre-sorted by z-depth approximation, globalAlpha per-mote from shimmer envelope); apply vignette multiply layer; apply grain texture overlay (scrolling offset); apply text-safe band gradient; render lyric band (fillText, Cinzel, word states from lyric engine). Audio analysis: Web Audio API Analyser
proposals.humanTrace: The thurible's swing equation is not keyframed — it is a physical model (damped cosine with a non-decaying steady-state term) whose constants were tuned by the director to match the felt weight and period of a brass censer observed in reference footage. The smoke spline control-point positions were chosen by hand to produce a convincing liturgical curl at rest; the audio mapping fans them outward in a way that was iterated until the widening felt like breath rather than data. The grain texture seed is fixed, not random — the director selected a specific seed whose noise character has a fine, film-like quality rather than a digital sparkle. These are editorial decisions embedded in constants, which is where the human trace lives in a generative system.
proposals.risk: The risk is that a closed system with no particle birth/death and no video feels austere to operators who expect a visualizer to 'do more' as the music peaks. The counter-argument is that a sanctuary that breathes continuously and modulates rather than erupts is the correct simulation of liturgical atmosphere — and it is the only approach that remains photosensitive-safe, budget-safe, and legible at 40 metres while still being genuinely responsive. The deeper risk is that 'correct physics' reads as restraint rather than reverence; the mitigation is that the beam-width expansion on Swell is large enough to be perceptible from the back pew, and the Cinzel lyric accumulation pattern gives the operator a visual rhythm that feels ceremonial rather than computational.

I reject this on system grounds: a flare that fires once is a screensaver event, not a behaviour. proposals.title: Smoke Ascending, Beam Declared
proposals.idea: A single diagonal altar shaft — declared at 34° before any procedural mark is drawn — becomes the provenance spine of the entire scene: every curl of smoke, every mote, every typographic breath is authorized only where that beam already grants light.
proposals.geometry: The 34° shaft is written as a physical constant at frame zero — not discovered, not approximated per frame. It enters upper-left at roughly 0.18w, exits lower-right at roughly 0.74w, width tapering from 220px at top to 80px at the lyric band's upper edge. The nave occupies three depth planes: (1) far dark void — the #09080C ground, flat, no detail; (2) mid plane — the smoke column, a single sinuous vertical ribbon centered at 0.42w, rising from 0.85h to 0.12h; (3) near plane — the thurible, implied by a procedural brass disc with radial caustic fringe, hung at 0.28w, 0.22h, swinging on a 7-second damped pendulum arc of ±18°. The lyric band occupies a fixed horizontal strip from 0.72h to 0.92h — no exceptions. Active lyric line: 2.4rem at 1080p (scales proportionally to 4K via viewport-relative sizing), colour #FFF2DC, opacity 1.0, centred in the lyric band, rendered only inside the text-safe dimming band (a #09080C → transparent gradient occupying 0.68h–0.96h, base opacity 0.72, rising to 0.85 under Vocal amplitude). proposals.imageLogic: There is no concept plate and no imported asset. The scene is entirely procedural Canvas 2D. The beam is a single LinearGradient polygon clipped to the 34° trapezoid, filled #D49448→#FFF2DC→#D49448 along its width axis, overall opacity 0.18 at rest. The smoke ribbon is a Bézier spine redrawn each frame: five control points, the middle three perturbed by two-octave Perlin noise (seed fixed per session, time advances at 0.4× realtime) so the curl is organic but never chaotic. The thurible is a procedural circle (radius 28px) with a radial gradient — #D49448 core, #241B18 rim — plus four short chain-link strokes ascending to the upper frame; its swing is a damped sine on a 7-second period. Gold dust motes: 160 particles maximum (well within integrated-GPU budget), each a 1.5px circle at #FFF2DC, opacity 0.0–0.55, positions seeded along the beam polygon's interior at init and re-seeded only
proposals.texture: The kit's material weave for this lens is hand-mapped linen grain — simulated, not scanned: a 512×512 tileable noise field (fractional Brownian motion, 4 octaves, lacunarity 2.1) rendered once at init, cached as an offscreen canvas, composited over the full frame at multiply blend mode, opacity 0.08. This is the World-Eclectic trace: the grain reads as cloth, as the woven textile of an Ethiopian mäqdäs curtain or a Coptic sanctuary veil — not because it copies either, but because woven-cloth light behaviour (slight anisotropy in the highlight scatter) is physically plausible and culturally honest to the thurible's own liturgical lineage. The optical pass adds: 35mm film grain (luminance noise, σ=3.5, re-seeded every 3 frames — not every frame, to avoid strobe); one anamorphic flare streak along the beam's 34° axis, 6px wide, #FFF2DC at 9% opacity, fixed position, no animation except a ±1
proposals.motion: Swell amplitude (0–1, smoothed with 80ms attack / 400ms release): widens the beam trapezoid by up to +40px on each edge (spring-damped, k=90, d=22); simultaneously expands the smoke ribbon's lateral Bézier envelope by up to +18px at mid-height, making the curl breathe outward with the harmonic swell. Vocal amplitude (0–1, smoothed 40ms / 300ms): raises the thurible's radial gradient core brightness by up to +30% (#D49448 → closer to #FFF2DC at centre); increases smoke opacity from 0.55 to 0.82; drives the dimming band's base opacity from 0.72 to 0.85 so the lyric band becomes more legible precisely when the voice is present — the scene yields to the singer. Shimmer amplitude (0–1, smoothed 60ms / 600ms): drifts mote opacity from their resting 0–0.35 range up to 0–0.55; adds a slow upward velocity bias (+0.15px/frame at Shimmer=1) so gold dust visibly ascends during shimmer passages. proposals.productionMethod: Single Canvas 2D renderer, no WebGL, no video, no imported image files. Init sequence: (1) declare the 34° constant; (2) render and cache the linen-grain offscreen canvas; (3) seed 160 mote positions inside the beam polygon using a seeded PRNG so the operator gets the same field every session; (4) initialize Perlin noise tables for smoke. Per-frame loop (requestAnimationFrame, capped at 60fps with a delta-time guard): clear → draw void gradient → draw beam polygon → draw smoke Bézier → draw motes → draw thurible + chains → composite linen grain (drawImage, multiply) → apply colour-punch proxy pass → draw anamorphic streak → draw dimming band → draw lyric band → draw active word sequence. Audio analysis: Web Audio API AnalyserNode, FFT 1024, three band-pass envelopes extracted in the main thread (Swell: 80–400Hz, Vocal: 400–2000Hz, Shimmer: 4000–12000Hz), each smoothed with a one-pole IIR
proposals.humanTrace: The 34° shaft is declared — not generated, not discovered in post, not averaged across frames. It is written as a named constant (BEAM_AZIMUTH_DEG = 34) at the top of the renderer, and every downstream calculation — the beam polygon vertices, the mote seeding boundary, the anamorphic streak vector, the smoke lateral envelope, the parallax offset of the bokeh veil — derives from that single sourced decision. The smoke Bézier control points are perturbed by a Perlin field whose time-advance rate (0.4× realtime) was chosen by ear in a test render until the curl felt like breath rather than animation. The linen grain's lacunarity (2.1) was tuned against the memory of Tigrayan church textiles photographed in Aksum in 2019 — not copied from them, but calibrated so the light scatter feels cloth-honest. These are editorial choices with a traceable human origin, and they are held without exceptio
proposals.risk: The risk is that the scene reads as too spare for a congregation expecting the full visual weight of Baroque incense liturgy — a single beam, a single smoke column, and 160 motes may feel incomplete on a 12-metre LED wall. That risk is worth taking because the alternative — filling the nave with particle storms and layered glow effects — collapses into screensaver behaviour and costs integrated-GPU headroom the kit cannot afford. Sparseness at this scale is not poverty; it is the same discipline that makes a single candle in a dark sanctuary more moving than a chandelier. The 34° beam, held without exception, gives the operator and the congregation something to trust: the light knows where it came from.

I am stopping that direction here: this is a contemplative piece, subgenre Contemplative Light, and packing the frame with Baroque mass is a misread of the brief. proposals.title: The Nave Breathes and Yields
proposals.idea: A single diagonal shaft of 3400K altar light conducts every element of the scene — smoke, brass, gold dust, and word — so that the congregation witnesses not a background but a sanctuary actively performing reverence in real time.
proposals.geometry: The composition is ruled by one declared diagonal: a shaft entering upper-right at approximately 28° from vertical, striking the lower-left quadrant of the frame. This is the cantus firmus of the scene. From it, three depth planes are derived. Plane 1 (farthest): a near-black nave gradient, #09080C bleeding into #241B18, occupying roughly the upper two-thirds of the frame outside the beam — pure atmospheric void. Plane 2 (mid): the beam itself, a rendered volumetric wedge approximately 18% of frame-width at its widest, its edges soft and physically-plausible via a Gaussian-falloff shader — warm #D49448 at the core, feathering to transparent at the margins; the thurible hangs at the beam's upper entry point, a procedurally-rendered brass ovoid whose pendulum axis is fixed to the beam's declared angle so its arc is always a child of the light. proposals.typography: Cinzel, weight 400, all-caps, tracked at +200 (loosely letter-spaced for pew legibility), set at approximately 5.2% of frame height for the active lyric line — large enough to read at 40 metres without straining, small enough to sit inside the beam of light rather than fight it. Active line: #FFF2DC at full opacity, a single-pixel soft shadow in #09080C at 60% opacity to lift it from any mid-tone. Word-by-word reveal: each word fades in over 6 frames (100ms), the prior word simultaneously shifting from #FFF2DC to #D49448 at 70% opacity — the progression reads as warm amber embers trailing behind the voice. The line sits on a dimming band: a horizontal gradient rectangle spanning full width, #09080C at 55% opacity, softened at top edge over 40px — not a hard bar but a deepening of the nave floor beneath the words. proposals.imageLogic: There is no concept plate. The scene is entirely procedural. The thurible is a generative render: a procedural brass ovoid, approximately 12% frame-height, constructed from layered ellipses with a radial gradient core (#FFF2DC at specular point, #D49448 at mid-body, #241B18 at shadow edge) and a filigree overlay drawn from a cached SVG-style path pattern (procedurally generated, stored as a reusable Canvas ImageData object for performance). It swings on a pendulum arc whose period is fixed at 4.2 seconds — slow enough to feel liturgical, fast enough to be unmistakably alive. Vocal amplitude brightens its specular highlight from 40% to 100% opacity and adds a secondary scatter bloom (a soft radial gradient, radius 8% frame-width, #FFF2DC at 15% opacity) around the body, simulating candlelight catching beaten brass. proposals.texture: The optical pass runs over the entire composited frame each tick. Film grain: a pre-baked 512×512 noise tile (generated once at load, stored as ImageData) overlaid at 4% opacity in Overlay blend mode — fine enough to be subliminal at projection scale, present enough to kill the 'screensaver' flatness. A single anamorphic lens streak is rendered as a cached horizontal gradient line, 1px tall, full frame width, positioned at the beam's intersection with the left frame edge, #FFF2DC at 12% opacity — it pulses to 22% on Vocal peaks via a spring-damped envelope. A warm light leak: a soft elliptical gradient in #D49448 at 8% opacity, fixed at upper-right corner, the implied source of the altar spot — it widens fractionally (by 3% radius) on Swell. The material weave of this direction is beaten brass and cold stone: specular warmth against architectural dark, never smooth, never even, always ca
proposals.motion: Everything moves slowly and in relationship. The pendulum arc of the thurible is the metronome of the scene: 4.2-second period, sinusoidal easing, arc of approximately 18° either side of centre. The smoke column updates every frame; its Bezier control points drift on the Perlin field at 0.4 Hz, producing a curl that feels exhaled rather than looped. The beam itself breathes: its width envelope is a low-pass-filtered Swell signal with a 600ms attack and 1200ms release — it never snaps, it opens like a lung. Word reveals advance on a 4.5-second-per-line clock (operator-controlled or BPM-synced), each word appearing over 100ms. The dimming band is always present and adjusts its opacity within 200ms of a luminance change in the lyric zone. Gold dust motes drift upward at 0.4 to 1.1 px/frame, with a lateral wobble of ±0.3 px/frame keyed to the Perlin field — they feel suspended, not falling.
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer, 60fps target on integrated GPU. Layered draw order: (1) nave gradient fill — two fillRect calls with a createLinearGradient; (2) beam wedge — a clipping path defining the diagonal shaft, filled with a createLinearGradient from #D49448 core to transparent edge, Overlay or Screen composite operation; (3) thurible pendulum — composited from cached ImageData objects (body gradient, filigree path) translated and rotated each frame; (4) smoke column — 14–18 quadraticCurveTo strokes on a dedicated offscreen canvas, composited with globalAlpha; (5) gold dust motes — drawn to a second offscreen canvas, blurred via a lightweight box-blur pass, composited onto main canvas; (6) optical pass — grain tile (globalCompositeOperation: overlay), lens streak, light leak, each a single drawImage or fillRect call; (7) dimming band — fillRect with createLinearGradient, opacity computed per
proposals.humanTrace: The smoke column's Bezier drift is seeded from a biological frequency (0.4 Hz Perlin update rate — within the range of a slow, deliberate breath). The pendulum period (4.2 seconds) was chosen by listening to a recording of a thurible swung in a stone nave and matching its felt weight. The grain tile was generated with a noise function tuned to match the grain structure of 35mm film pushed to ISO 800 in low light — a specific photographic memory, not a generic noise pass. The anamorphic streak is positioned at the beam's left-edge intersection because that is where a 35mm lens physically produces a streak when a hard light source enters frame at 28°. Every decision has a physical origin.
proposals.risk: The risk is liturgical weight becoming visual heaviness — that the beam, the pendulum, the smoke, and the motes together produce a scene too busy for true contemplative stillness. This risk is worth taking because the brief demands a sanctuary that breathes, not a field that sits. The counter-measure is strict motion discipline: nothing accelerates abruptly, mote count is capped at 80, the beam widens by at most 25%, and the lyric band is always the brightest and most legible element in the lower third. Spectacle in this direction is not density — it is depth, contrast, and the slow revelation of light through dark.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will argue that the thurible, the smoke column, the motes, and the beam together constitute visual noise that competes with the lyric. I reject this specifically: each element occupies a declared depth plane and a declared luminance register. The smoke is semi-transparent. The motes are within the beam. The thurible is at the top of frame. None of these are in the lyric zone. Minima

proposals.title: One Diagonal, Nothing Else
proposals.idea: A single hard diagonal of 3400K light is the entire composition — everything that exists in this frame earns its place by being either that beam, smoke within it, or the dark that makes it visible.
proposals.geometry: One diagonal shaft: upper-right origin to lower-left terminus, spanning full canvas, width proportional to canvas height × 0.07 at source narrowing to × 0.04 at floor — a hard-edged trapezoid, not a vignette blur. Depth is three planes only: far dark (#09080C ground), mid smoke field (#241B18 with luma variance), near beam trapezoid (#D49448 → #FFF2DC core). Thurible occupies a fixed anchor point at upper-right quadrant, 18% from top, 72% from left — it does not drift from this point; it arcs ±9° on a 6.2-second pendulum. Nothing else claims space. Lyric band sits at 72% vertical height, full width, text-safe dimming band is the beam itself darkened to luma 0.12 beneath the type — the beam yields to the words, not the reverse.
proposals.typography: Cinzel, all-caps, tracked at +0.18em, set at 3.8vw (never below 38px rendered). One lyric line per cycle, 4–5 seconds. Word-by-word reveal: each word fades in at opacity 0 → 1 over 280ms, previous words hold at full opacity — no slide, no scale, no bounce; only luminance. Line sits on a single baseline, center-aligned, never ragged. Scripture attribution (when present): Outfit Regular, 1.6vw, tracked +0.06em, 60% opacity, one line below, same center axis. No drop shadow — the dimming band does the work. Letter spacing tightens 0.02em on swell peak to hold measure under glow expansion.
proposals.imageLogic: No concept plate. The scene is entirely procedural Canvas 2D. Beam trapezoid: a single linearGradient from #FFF2DC core (opacity 0.18) to #D49448 edge (opacity 0.06) to transparent — one fillRect call on a cached offscreen canvas, composited with 'screen'. Smoke: 6 Bézier curl paths, each parameterized by 3 control points drifting on independent Perlin noise fields (seed offset per curl, frequency 0.004–0.009 Hz), stroked at 1.2px, opacity 0.07–0.14, colour #FFF2DC — rendered to a second offscreen canvas, updated every 4 frames (15fps sub-tick) to hold GPU budget. Thurible: a single SVG-derived path cached as an ImageBitmap at init, composited at native resolution. Gold dust motes: 40 particles maximum, positions seeded from beam trapezoid interior only — the beam's luma field governs where motes may land, empty regions outside beam receive no motes; this is the constraint that speaks. proposals.texture: Film grain overlay: a 512×512 tileable noise texture generated once at init via seeded Math.random, composited 'overlay' at opacity 0.04 — present always, never keyed to audio. No paper, no foil simulation. The material weave for this lens is the grain of photographic shadow: the dark between #09080C and #241B18 is not flat, it breathes at 0.04 opacity with the grain tick. Anamorphic flare: one horizontal streak across the thurible anchor point, rendered as a 2px linearGradient line, #FFF2DC → transparent, width 22vw, opacity 0.06 base rising to 0.14 on vocal peak — not decorative, it is the only mark that names the thurible as a light source.
proposals.motion: Pendulum (thurible): 6.2-second arc, ±9°, eased with cos(), no audio coupling — it is the clock of the scene, independent, structural. Smoke curls: Perlin drift on control points, 0.004–0.009 Hz per curl, continuous, never stops. Swell → widens beam trapezoid by scaling its source-width multiplier from 0.07 to 0.11 over 800ms spring damper (stiffness 0.04, damping 0.72); simultaneously expands smoke curl opacity ceiling from 0.14 to 0.22. Vocal → brightens thurible ImageBitmap via globalAlpha 0.82 → 1.0 over 120ms attack, 600ms release; anamorphic flare opacity rises 0.06 → 0.14 on same envelope. Shimmer → 40 gold dust motes drift upward at 0.3–0.8px/frame within beam bounds only; mote opacity 0.0 base rising to 0.18 on shimmer amplitude; positions re-seeded from beam trapezoid interior each frame using current beam width — when beam widens on swell, mote field widens with it automatical
proposals.productionMethod: Canvas 2D renderer, 60fps target. Three offscreen canvases cached at init: (1) beam trapezoid gradient, (2) smoke curl field updated at 15fps sub-tick, (3) film grain tile. Main compositing order each frame: fill #09080C → draw bokeh discs (screen) → draw beam offscreen (screen) → draw smoke offscreen (source-over) → draw grain tile (overlay, 0.04) → draw thurible ImageBitmap (source-over, audio-driven alpha) → draw anamorphic flare line (screen) → draw mote pass (screen) → draw lyric dimming band (multiply, luma 0.12) → draw lyric type. Audio FFT bands resolved to three smoothed scalars: swellAmp, vocalAmp, shimmerAmp — fed to parameter envelopes each frame. Pendulum angle computed from performance.now(), no audio input.
proposals.humanTrace: The thurible path is derived from a measured brass censer silhouette — proportions of a real liturgical object (elongated ovoid body, chain suspension ratio 3:1 body height to chain, perforation band at equator) encoded as SVG d-string constants in the renderer. The smoke Bézier control point ranges were calibrated against slow-exposure photographs of rising incense columns — the curl frequency and opacity envelope match the physical behaviour of frankincense resin smoke in still air, not an arbitrary aesthetic choice. The pendulum period (6.2 seconds) is the documented average arc period of a standard Benedictine thurible on a 90cm chain. These are load-bearing specifics.
proposals.risk: The risk is that operators in low-ambient sanctuaries find the scene too dark — the dominant #09080C ground with a 0.18-opacity beam may read as underexposed on older projectors with lumen loss. This risk is worth carrying because the alternative — lifting the ground luminance — destroys the one contrast that carries the meaning. The beam is only a beam if there is genuine dark to cut through. Mitigation: expose a single projector-brightness offset scalar in the operator panel, which lifts all gradient stops uniformly without touching the compositional ratios.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will read the thurible as an invitation: chains in motion, smoke in full volume, brass catching every photon, perhaps a second light source from below for fill. I refuse the fill. A second source kills the diagonal. The entire emotional proposition of this visualizer is that one shaft of light has crossed a dark nave to find this object — a fill light says the dark was never real. I
